content.headline: AI turns meetings into immediate, editable artifacts
content.subtitle: Doc Co‑Creation Agent in Teams to power Copilot usage and make Teams the OS of work

story: Situation: establish current business-critical role of documents and Teams
visual_design: 2-column framework: left = 'Work Runs on Artifacts', right = 'Teams is the Collaboration Hub'; use simple iconography, no complex charts.

content.headline: Enterprise impact still depends on PPT and Word artifacts
content.subtitle: Meetings and chats only create value once turned into specs, decks, and docs
content.speaker_intent: Align leadership that our revenue, decisions, and customer impact are mediated through Office artifacts, not just conversations.

sections.title: Artifacts drive execution and business outcomes

bullets.text: Critical decisions, funding, and execution plans are documented in specs, slide decks, and written proposals.
Over 30M PowerPoint files are created every day, underscoring how central slides are to how enterprises think and decide.
Word and PPT are the de facto languages of enterprise storytelling and alignment.

sections.title: Teams already concentrates collaboration and context

bullets.text: Teams is where meetings happen, chats unfold, and files are shared and discussed.
Meeting audio/video, chat histories, and shared documents together capture the richest picture of user intent.
Yet the final artifacts that matter (PPTX, DOCX) are still produced outside the live collaboration flow.

story: Complication: quantify the productivity and value leakage of manual document creation
visual_design: Cause-and-effect flow diagram from 'Live discussion' → 'Manual translation' → 'Delayed artifacts' → 'Slower execution'; annotate with bullet callouts.

content.headline: Manual document creation after meetings drains productivity
content.subtitle: Human bottlenecks slow the conversion of spoken intent into tool-ready outputs
content.speaker_intent: Create urgency by framing current workflows as a structural productivity loss and risk to Copilot value realization.

sections.title: Meeting outputs are stuck in a legacy workflow

bullets.text: Historically, the only meeting output was text minutes; today, work requires structured artifacts across PPT, ADO, specs, and whiteboards.
Modern meetings still mostly produce raw text or unstructured notes that require significant post-processing.
Participants cannot both engage in a live discussion and operate multiple tools fast enough to generate structured outputs in real time.

sections.title: The cost: time drain, delay, and lost quality

bullets.text: Employees spend disproportionate time on formatting, layout, and style instead of high-value strategic thinking.
The 'blank page' problem makes it hard to turn dense meeting content into concise, coherent slide narratives.
Non-designers struggle to achieve polished, enterprise-ready aesthetics, leading to inconsistent quality and frustration.

story: Complication + Question: introduce competitive and market pressure, raise strategic question
visual_design: 2x2 matrix: X-axis = 'Use of enterprise context', Y-axis = 'Fidelity of output'; plot 'Generic summarizers', 'Gamma', 'Gemini', and 'Teams today'; highlight white space in top-right as opportunity.

content.headline: Competitors target AI slide creation while we leave a gap
content.subtitle: Gamma’s 70M users and Gemini pressure show demand for AI-first content generation
content.speaker_intent: Highlight that inaction risks ceding the highest-value AI use case to competitors and under-monetizing Copilot.

sections.title: Market signals show explosive demand for AI-generated slides

bullets.text: Gamma, a dedicated AI slide and doc generator, has already attracted over 70M users.
Generative AI tools are shifting expectations from manual editing to direct content generation from ideas and discussions.
Users increasingly expect 'one-click' conversion from intent to polished slides and docs.

sections.title: Our current position underutilizes our unique assets

bullets.text: Copilot and PowerPoint already support PPT generation, but they operate largely on static prompts and files, not live meeting context.
Teams today does not fully exploit its access to fresh meeting audio/video, chats, shared files, and histories to generate artifacts in real time.
This creates a 'crisis of inaction': we risk losing the killer AI use case to point solutions while owning the richest data and Office formats.
How do we turn every Teams meeting into an automatic generator of high-fidelity Office artifacts, strengthening Copilot value and our competitive moat?

story: Answer: introduce the core solution and its transformative promise
visual_design: Before/After bridge chart: left = 'Today: Talk → Notes → Manual Docs'; right = 'Future: Talk → AI Agent → PPTX/DOCX/ADO in real time'; center arrow labeled with punchline.

content.headline: Doc co‑creation agent in Teams turns spoken intent into artifacts
content.subtitle: AI generates PPT and Word directly from live meetings, chats, and channel context
content.speaker_intent: Land the core idea crisply and position it as a natural extension of Teams and Copilot.

bullets.text: Build a Teams-native doc co‑creation agent that listens to meetings and reads chats and shared files to generate PPTX and DOCX automatically.
Unify in-meeting discussion and document creation into a single workflow, enabling artifacts to be created during or immediately after the meeting.
Extend the same content generation engine to other Microsoft content platforms such as SharePoint over time.
Spoken intent becomes immediate, tool-ready output inside Teams.

story: Answer: zoom into user experience and workflow inside Teams
visual_design: User journey swimlane with 3 phases: 'During meeting', 'Immediately after', 'Collaborative refinement'; annotate where 'PPT Maker' panel and preview window appear.

content.headline: Teams-native PPT Maker unifies discussion and document creation
content.subtitle: Interactive co‑creation panel plus live slide preview embedded in the meeting experience
content.speaker_intent: Help leadership visualize the experience and understand why it must live in Teams, not just in standalone Office apps.

bullets.text: A 'PPT Maker' panel appears within Teams, enabling participants to interact with the agent during the meeting.
The agent listens to the evolving conversation, captures decisions and key points, and proposes slide structures in real time.
A preview window shows draft slides (e.g., 'Advanced AI-Driven Speech Recognition & Enhancement System') as they are generated.
Users can navigate thumbnails, enter full-screen mode, and quickly review or adjust generated slides immediately after the meeting.
Teams’ collaboration model allows multiple users to review, edit, and refine the document together in real time.
The same agent can generate Word specs or other 'Smart Docs' using the same meeting and channel context.

sections.title: Why Teams is the right home

bullets.text: Teams uniquely combines live audio/video, chat, and shared files, giving the agent a multi-modal grounding competitors cannot match.

story: Answer Deep Dive: explain the technical workflow and feasibility
visual_design: Process flow diagram (consulting-style) with 4 main blocks: Orchestrator → Data Miner → Content Creator (Weaver + Structurer) → Assembler & Engine; use a Sankey-style flow or left-to-right process chart.

content.headline: Orchestrated AI pipeline makes high-fidelity artifacts technically feasible
content.subtitle: Dispatcher, Miner, Weaver, Structurer, and Assembler collaborate to produce PPTX/DOCX/HTML/MP4
content.speaker_intent: Demonstrate that this is an engineered system with clear components, not a vague AI wish list.

sections.title: 1. Orchestrator plans tasks based on user intent

bullets.text: A Dispatcher interprets user input (requested slides, context, instructions) and plans the sequence of tasks.
It determines which enterprise data sources to query and what artifacts to generate.

sections.title: 2. Miner extracts facts from enterprise data

bullets.text: The Miner pulls 'Facts' from meetings, chats, and documents into a structured Content Pool.
Content is organized into Atoms such as architecture details, metrics, and code snippets for precise reuse.

sections.title: 3. Weaver and Structurer turn facts into narratives

bullets.text: The Weaver synthesizes extracted facts into coherent narration aligned to the meeting’s storyline.
The Structurer organizes that narration into slides and chapters, ensuring systematic narrative flow.

sections.title: 4. Assembler and Engine finalize layout and format

bullets.text: The Assembler applies layout and style, targeting a polished, enterprise-ready aesthetic.
An Engine layer (HTML, FFMPEG, python-pptx) outputs final artifacts in HTML, PPTX, DOCX, or MP4 formats.

story: Answer: articulate the differentiated moat vs. competitors and internal alternatives
visual_design: Moat flywheel diagram: 'Teams meetings & data' → 'AI doc co‑creation' → 'More usage & data gravity' → 'Stronger Copilot value & retention' → back to 'Teams meetings & data'; annotate with advantages vs. Zoom/Slack/Gamma.

content.headline: Microsoft’s integrated stack creates a defensible doc co‑creation moat
content.subtitle: Teams + Office formats + Copilot enable a solution competitors cannot easily copy
content.speaker_intent: Reassure leadership that this investment deepens our strategic moat, not just adds another feature.

sections.title: We own the full stack competitors rely on

bullets.text: Teams holds the meeting data (audio/video, chats, shared files, histories).
Microsoft controls the file standards (PPTX, DOCX) that define enterprise artifacts.
Copilot provides the AI layer to interpret intent and generate content.

sections.title: Competitors cannot match seamless, native Office outputs

bullets.text: Zoom and Slack can summarize meetings but cannot natively generate high-fidelity, editable Office documents as seamlessly.
Third-party tools like Gamma generate slides but operate outside Teams and without deep access to enterprise context.
Our agent uses fresh meeting knowledge plus chats and files to ground outputs in real enterprise data.
Unlike generic Copilot in PowerPoint, the Teams agent is context-rich, using live conversations and collaboration history.
We remain open to integrating with existing services like Societas where they are ready, but Teams is the orchestration hub.

story: Answer: quantify business value levers—monetization, stickiness, data gravity
visual_design: 3-part value framework (horizontal): 'Monetize Copilot' / 'Deepen moat' / 'Increase Teams stickiness & data gravity'; under each, 2–3 concise bullets.

content.headline: Doc co‑creation unlocks Copilot monetization and Teams stickiness
content.subtitle: One-click PPT becomes the killer app that keeps work and data in our ecosystem
content.speaker_intent: Connect the solution directly to revenue (ARPU uplift), retention, and strategic positioning.

bullets.text: ‘One-click to PPT’ is a tangible, high-value feature that directly justifies the $30/month Copilot for Microsoft 365 license.
It moves AI from 'nice to have' to 'essential for workflow' by solving a daily, painful task for knowledge workers.
Ecosystem advantage: we uniquely combine Teams, Office formats, and Copilot into a tightly integrated experience.
Hard to copy: competitors can summarize meetings but cannot generate native, high-fidelity PPTX/DOCX tied to live collaboration.

sections.title: 3. Increase platform stickiness and data gravity

bullets.text: By moving document creation inside Teams, we transform it from a communication tool into the OS of work.
Users never have to leave Teams to create or edit artifacts, increasing time-in-app and reducing churn.
If the best way to draft a document is to 'have a meeting about it,' users are incentivized to host more discussions and store more data in our ecosystem.

story: Answer: acknowledge key challenges and proposed mitigations to de-risk
visual_design: Risk vs. Mitigation table: left column = 'Challenge', right column = 'Mitigation approach'; 3–4 rows.

content.headline: Key challenges are known and can be systematically de-risked
content.subtitle: WOW quality, aesthetic evaluation, and narrative coherence require focused investment
content.speaker_intent: Show that we are realistic about execution risks and have a plan to address them.

bullets.text: Achieving a 'WOW' effect in generated slides is difficult and requires robust aesthetic evaluation.
Building systematic, coherent narratives from noisy meeting inputs is non-trivial.
Dataset construction for layout, style, and narrative quality is a significant effort.
Current resource limitations in SOX CMD make it hard for the team to own this project end-to-end.
Invest in dedicated design resources to define aesthetic evaluation metrics and target enterprise-grade styles.
Leverage Teams’ rich telemetry and existing documents to bootstrap datasets for narrative and layout training.
Structure the project as a focused, cross-functional effort with clear ownership and milestones.

story: Answer: clarify resource ask and what leadership’s decision will enable
visual_design: Simple Gantt-style bar or milestone list for phases (e.g., Prototype, Pilot, GA) aligned with resource blocks; no dates invented—leave timing conceptual.

content.headline: Focused investment will convert Teams’ advantages into a flagship AI experience
content.subtitle: Request: 6 devs (3 senior+) plus designer support to deliver a WOW co‑creation agent
content.speaker_intent: Make a concrete ask and tie it to the impact and feasibility already established.

bullets.text: Engineering: 6 developers, including at least 3 senior engineers, to own orchestrator, mining, content creation, and integration layers.
Design: dedicated designer(s) to define visual standards and aesthetic evaluation metrics for PPT and Word outputs.
A Teams-integrated doc co‑creation agent that showcases Copilot’s value in a daily, high-visibility workflow.
A differentiated, defensible feature that strengthens Teams as the OS of work and increases Copilot ARPU justification.
A reusable content generation engine extensible to SharePoint and other Microsoft applications.
A relatively small, focused team can unlock a flagship AI use case anchored in our core ecosystem.

story: ending: crystallize decision and close on vision
visual_design: Decision slide with 2–3 bullet decision points and a short vision statement; simple layout.

content.headline: Decision: fund Teams doc co‑creation to make meetings produce work, not work about work
content.subtitle: Approve resources to build the AI agent that turns every Teams meeting into immediate, high-fidelity Office artifacts
